description: Least privilege for the one Onyx window. The webview may listen to and emit events (the three onyx:// streams of SPEC §3.2 plus onyx://client-log of §13), drag / double-click-maximise the custom title bar of §4, and drive the three window buttons that title bar draws on Windows and Linux (macOS keeps its own traffic lights) — nothing else. Everything the app can actually do goes through its own #[tauri::command] surface (SPEC §3.1), which the webview cannot widen. The dialog / opener / log / single-instance / window-state plugins are driven from Rust only, so no plugin permission is granted here at all: a compromised renderer gets no file picker, no shell, no URL opener and no second window. `tauri-plugin-fs` is not registered at all any more — Onyx reads files with std::fs from Rust, so the webview has no file system to be given access to. `core:default` used to be listed instead, which additionally handed out every window/webview/monitor getter, the menu and tray builders, image-from-path and the devtools toggle — none of which the front end calls.
